## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 8e5ee782690175e9cfb9a

asoning

**(1) Investigation:** The fix commit (3ee6d03) describes two specific logical bugs in the `words` FTS3 table id-off
setting scheme: (a) `(2 << 32)` in `MmsProvider.java` evaluates to `2` due to Java's int-shift-amount modulo-32 r
ule, and (b) `populateWordsTable` (used on DB upgrade) never added the mms-part offset at all. I used `git log -p --follow` on `MmsProvider.java
` and `MmsSmsDatabaseHelper.java` to trace every historical change to the `WordsTable.ID`/`populateWordsTable`/`2 << 32` code, then located

the earliest commit that introduced this logic.

**(2) The introducing commit:** `8e5ee782690175e9cfb9a37f600f207b952ba8a6` ("search work",

Jan 2010) is the commit that originally introduced the entire `words` FTS3 table feature, including:
- In `MmsProvider.java`'s part insert path: `cv.put(Telephony.Mm

sSms.WordsTable.ID, (2 << 32) + rowId);` — the exact buggy int-shift expression called out in the fix.
- In `MmsSmsDatabaseHelper.java`'s `populateWordsTable`, the
mms/part loop: `cv.put(Telephony.MmsSms.WordsTable.ID, id);` with no offset added at all, and even incorrectly sets `TABLE_ID` to `1` (s

ms) instead of `2` (mms) for part rows — exactly the second bug described ("didn't add the offset at all").

Both defects have persisted unchanged through the

entire history up to the fix commit; I found no intermediate commit that touched or altered this offsetting logic.

**(3) Evidence:**
`git show 8e5ee782...` for both files shows the code verbatim matching the bug description in the fix commit's message word-for-word (the `2 << 32` comment/

expression, and the missing offset plus wrong `TABLE_ID` in `populateWordsTable`). No other commit in the file history modifies these lines before the fix commit itself.

I
'm confident in this attribution — the buggy expressions are byte-for-byte traceable to this single original commit with no intervening changes.
